papers.title: Premature Occlusal Contacts Induce MRONJ in Osseointegrated Dental Implants: An Experimental In Vivo Study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a debilitating condition associated with antiresorptive agents (ARAs) and can occur around well-osseointegrated dental implants. Although implant presence-triggered osteonecrosis (IPTO) has been primarily linked to bacteria-related peri-implantitis, whether occlusal trauma contributes to IPTO remains unclear. Therefore, this study developed a novel premature occlusal contact (POC) mouse implant model to evaluate the effect of occlusal trauma on MRONJ development around osseointegrated implants. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Eighteen mice underwent bilateral maxillary first molar extraction followed by immediate implant placement. After a 3-week healing period to allow osseointegration, mice were randomized to receive intravenous zoledronic acid (ZOL, 125 μg/kg) or saline vehicle (Veh) twice weekly (n = 9 per group). One week later, POC was induced in a split-mouth design by applying composite resin to one implant, whereas the contralateral implant served as a control. After 5 weeks of occlusal loading, mice were euthanized for μCT and histological analyses. RESULTS: μCT analysis revealed that POC reduced radiographic bone-to-implant contact (rBIC) in both Veh- and ZOL-treated mice. POC significantly increased empty lacunae around the implant neck in Veh-treated mice, whereas in ZOL-treated mice, POC induced extensive circumferential bone necrosis around the implant, accompanied by increased macrophage infiltration. No significant differences in peptidoglycan (PGN)-positive signals were observed among the experimental groups. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that POC contributes to peri-implant osteonecrosis under ZOL treatment, supporting occlusal trauma as an important local factor in MRONJ development around osseointegrated dental implants.

papers.title: SLoSa: Small, Low-Power, and Safe Foundation Models for Robotic Task Planning
papers.abstract: Safe robotic task planning requires planners that can reliably achieve task goals while satisfying safety constraints. Classical planners search over explicit symbolic task representations and can provide formal guarantees with respect to encoded safety constraints, but require rigid input formats. Their computational cost also increases rapidly with the search space. In contrast, large language models (LLMs) offer flexible task interfaces and strong generalization capabilities, but they are large, power-hungry, and pre-trained with little robot-specific safety data and knowledge. Thus, they can be difficult to deploy locally on robotic systems with limited resources. To address these limitations, we present SLoSa, a neuro-symbolic compression and fine-tuning framework for training foundation-model-based robotic task planners with Small size, Low power demand, and Safety awareness. The framework first constructs a safety-aware dataset using classical planners, an advanced teacher LLM, and formal verifiers, followed by two training stages: supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning guided by a verification-based reward machine to enforce safety alignment. We evaluate SLoSa across four Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) domains, two household simulation environments, local edge platforms, and a desktop robotic arm. Across the PDDL tasks, verifier-guided post-training raises the success rate of compact 4B-14B planners to 70.5-76.0%, while INT4 deployment on a Jetson Orin requires 17.85-26.41 W of average power. Results in household simulators and on the physical robot further demonstrate the applicability of SLoSa across diverse robotic task settings.

papers.title: Self-Improving Agents with World Model Predictive Paths
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to interact with environments and improve their decisions during deployment. However, how anticipating future outcomes and drawing on accumulated interaction experience can jointly support decision-making remains underexplored. We propose a test-time framework, inspired by Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control, that combines multi-branch predictive analysis with experience-based adaptation. At each step, the agent proposes multiple candidate actions and imagines their outcomes with a world model, so that alternatives can be compared without being executed in the environment. Since language environments provide neither explicit dynamics nor costs, the predicted outcomes are evaluated for task progress and risk, and MPPI-style weights over the resulting costs guide the final decision. A dual-branch experience memory enables self-improvement: the planner branch refines candidate generation and action selection, while the world model branch improves next-observation prediction. Experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld across three backbones demonstrate the strong overall performance of our method and the effectiveness of experience-guided predictive control. Our code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Auditing Conformal Prediction for Language Models Under Inference-Time Model Shift
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) for language models is typically evaluated under a matched protocol, in which calibration and deployment use the same post-training inference configuration, such as quantization mode and inference temperature. In deployment, these choices often differ from those used at calibration to meet memory or throughput constraints or serving policies. We argue that this exposes a limitation in current CP evaluation protocols for language models. We formalize the underlying phenomenon as inference-time model shift: a change in the conformal score distribution induced by inference configuration rather than by the input--label distribution, and theoretically characterize how it breaks split-conformal exchangeability even when the task distribution and trained model are unchanged. We then evaluate its consequences across 8 language models, 4 finite-label benchmarks, and 12 inference configurations. We find that matched evaluation can substantially overstate deployment-time coverage, and that the effect is heterogeneous across models and datasets. We argue that inference configuration should be reported as a first-class experimental axis in CP evaluations for language-model systems.

papers.title: DualHeads: Reward-tilted few-step diffusion made simple
papers.abstract: Distilled diffusion models generate high-quality images in a few sampling steps, but aligning them with task requirements and human preferences is difficult. Methods developed for multi-step diffusion models rely on differentiable rewards, or on score fields and stochastic trajectories that distilled generators may lack. We ask whether a few-step generator can be adapted using only external reward evaluations and reference samples, and show that two binary classifiers suffice. Our method, DualHeads, implements them as lightweight heads on a frozen diffusion backbone. The reward head learns which samples of the same prompt score higher, the reference head separates reference images from generated ones, and the generator maximizes a weighted sum of their logits. When the heads are optimal, this objective is KL-regularized maximization of the learned reward, and the ratio of head weights sets the regularization strength. Empirically, with both rule-based and model-based rewards, a few-step DualHeads generator reaches task rewards close to those of 40-step reinforcement learning methods while preserving image quality, at no extra inference cost. We hope that this simple and elegant dual-head formulation will help advance few-step reward-tilted generation.

papers.title: WorldStream: Streaming Interactive 3D Worlds with Hierarchical Planning and Persistent State
papers.abstract: We present WorldStream, an open-ended 3D world model with three simultaneous capabilities: it extends playable terrain beyond any pre-specified map, acts on open-ended language in the running world, and restores visited places with their edits. A hierarchical planner over a typed decision model emits structured decision state: Macro fixes settlement, ecology, transport, and hydrological structure across a group of tiles; Micro specializes that contract into tile semantics under measured terrain and accepted neighbor commitments. Deterministic local code compiles accepted plans into terrain, roads, settlements, vegetation, and entities. Streaming separates their reach: plans run ahead along the predicted corridor, compilation only where movement will soon need it, geometry behind the user released. One world record retains plans, seeds, object identities and mutable state, boundary commitments, and edits by attribute, revised as the user advances and edits; returning tiles recompile from it. The same record grounds interaction: the model acts on existing entities, including stateful NPCs that update as they act, edits the present region, or attaches intent to unplanned regions. Together they yield a world expanding under bounded budgets, connected across independently planned tiles, and interactive.

papers.title: Brittle by Design? Multi-Scenario Reinforcement Learning for Robust Mission Coordination in Systems of Systems
papers.abstract: As systems engineering (SE) shifts from monolithic systems to Systems of Systems, Mission Engineering (ME) has emerged as a new line of thinking in SE. Mission environments are uncertain and dynamic, and outcomes depend on how mission assets interact with them, rendering static architectures brittle and calling for flexible yet analytically rigorous ME approaches. We propose an intelligent mission coordination methodology integrating high-fidelity digital mission models with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for adaptive task allocation. Using a Digital Engineering (DE) infrastructure comprising a digital mission model and agent-based simulation, we formulate mission tactics management as a Markov Decision Process and train an RL coordinator with Proximal Policy Optimization to map mission states to tactical actions from realized outcomes. An aerial firefighting mission with three scenarios demonstrates the approach. First, all trained coordinators significantly outperform random and heuristic baselines. Second, single-scenario coordinators can be brittle: the coordinator trained on the more forgiving scenario degrades to random tactics performance in more demanding scenarios, whereas the demanding-scenario coordinator retains most of its advantage when transferred. Third, within the same training budget, a coordinator trained on both scenarios concurrently matches the scenario-specific coordinators in their own scenarios and significantly outperforms every other policy. Sensitivity analyses on ignition location, weather, scenario, and training curricula show that the variability represented during training shapes post-deployment performance. This proof of concept shows DE-enabled mission simulations combined with RL offer a reusable methodology for improving ME practice, which can be extended to fleet design and selection from a mission-first perspective.

papers.title: ArcFlow: Training Flow Policies for Multiple Solver Budgets
papers.abstract: Flow-matching policies adjust inference cost through the number of solver steps, but reinforcement learning at a single fixed solver budget can hide degradation at cheaper deployment budgets and even erase useful one-step behavior present in a pretrained policy. We introduce Action-Ratio-Clip Flow (ArcFlow), a deployment-aware algorithm for training one flow policy across a specified range of solver budgets. ArcFlow combines action-aligned supervision, budget exposure, and worst-budget checkpoint selection. For reconstruction objectives, its bridge aggregates temporal probes into one surrogate ratio and one PPO-style clip per action, with a boundary residual exactly equal to deployed one-step reconstruction error. Cycling exposes the shared field to the deployment range, and selection optimizes its performance floor. For native velocity objectives, multi-budget endpoint supervision applies the same principle without replacing the native update. Both realizations preserve the architecture and deployment-time cost. Across DM Control, manipulation, and locomotion, ArcFlow attains the highest mean one-step return among five flow-policy baselines on 25 of 30 tasks under each method's reported training settings. Component studies identify complementary improvements from boundary supervision, the fixed-grid bridge, budget exposure, and deployment selection. These results establish deployment-budget-aware training as an effective route to strong low-step control with one policy serving multiple inference costs.

papers.title: Second Thoughts: Exploring and Planning through Comparative Imagination in World Models
papers.abstract: World models let agents compare imagined outcomes before acting, but an agent must still decide which alternatives to explore and when a proposed plan should replace its learned policy. We introduce SDI (Sibling Disagreement in Imagination), which connects these decisions through a shared actor-based reference. SDI compares action sequences imagined from the same model state, using repeated rollouts of the actor's own sequence to measure variation under fixed behavior. This reference scales both the spread across candidate returns, which provides an exploration signal, and a proposed plan's predicted advantage, which governs action acceptance. The agent executes a planned action when its advantage exceeds the reference variability by a fixed factor; otherwise, it follows the actor. SDI reuses the base agent's world model, actor, and critic without requiring an additional disagreement ensemble. Exploration and planning guide training data collection, while evaluation uses the learned actor alone. Across Meta-World, Adroit, and DM-Control, SDI achieves a higher observed task-average score than every compared baseline in each suite and matches or exceeds the strongest baseline's performance on 15 of 18 tasks. Component ablations and robustness analyses further examine the roles of exploration, planning exposure, and action acceptance. Paired evaluations from identical simulator states show that the gate improves both recovery from actor failures and preservation of successful behavior relative to ungated planning, while substantially reducing return degradation. Together, these results support comparing imagined alternatives against a shared actor reference as a unified approach to exploring and planning with world models.

papers.title: Complexity-Aware Surgical Video Reasoning Segmentation with Digital Twin and Context Memory
papers.abstract: Conventional surgical segmentation relies on closed-set categories or explicit text queries, which cannot resolve implicit queries that require reasoning about workflows, instrument functions, and temporal relationships. To address these limitations, we propose SurgReasonSeg, a complexity-aware method that brings reasoning segmentation over digital twin (DT) representations to surgical video. Specifically, SurgReasonSeg constructs DT representations from surgical foundation models and trains two low-rank adapters (LoRA) of one large language model with reinforcement learning (RL), each specialized for a different query complexity. A lightweight router, also trained with RL, selects between the two adapters to balance latency against accuracy. SurgReasonSeg also sets the temporal context with an adaptive sliding window conditioned on query complexity and workflow phase, and retrieves relevant historical cases from a surgical context memory by workflow similarity and procedural relevance. We further introduce EndoVis-ReasonSeg, a surgical reasoning segmentation benchmark with 1,460 training and 961 test samples across semantic, spatial, and temporal categories. On EndoVis-ReasonSeg, SurgReasonSeg improves J&F over the strongest baseline, ReSurgSAM2, by 0.178, 0.237, and 0.297 on semantic, spatial, and temporal queries, and it also achieves the best results on the Ref-EndoVis17 and Ref-EndoVis18 referring segmentation benchmarks. A backbone-matched attribution protocol separates the contribution of the upstream segmenter from that of the reasoning modules. Our method runs at 18.8 FPS averaged over the query distribution, enabling real-time reasoning segmentation in surgical videos.

papers.title: Understanding the Inner Workings of a State-Space Foundation Model for Limit Order Books
papers.abstract: Autoregressive foundation models offer state-of-the-art capabilities to simulate the market by generating the message flow of limit order books (LOBs). Yet, without understanding their inner workings, research directions are hard to narrow and practical use in real-world trading environments remains uncertain. This study therefore asks what these models actually learn about market microstructure. We find that, similarly to games where sequence models build an internal representation of the board, an 8.2M-parameter Mamba-3 state-space model trained autoregressively on the tokenized message stream of eight large-cap US equities learns an internal representation of the market and its dynamics. In particular, order-flow imbalance, a central driver of short-horizon price moves, is decodable at $R^2 \approx 0.59$, far above controls and baselines. This representation extends to unseen stocks, suggesting that these models learn general representations rather than ticker-specific patterns. The model also generalizes across metrics beyond order-flow imbalance: results hold across traded volume and volatility. Additionally, the representation is causally steerable: pushing the state along a feature's axis shifts the model's next-message beliefs as that feature implies, monotonically in dose, consistent with the emergence of a world model.

papers.title: SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training
papers.abstract: When training LLMs to code with reinforcement learning, reward hacking is often detectable but difficult to prevent, since (a) environment hardening is increasingly difficult as training environments grow more complex; and (b) training-time interventions incentivize models to obfuscate hacking behavior to bypass detection.   We instead study whether we can predict when detectable reward hacking becomes dominant before executing an RL run, enabling us to select lower-risk recipes in advance. We find that the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset, which varies substantially across training recipes and repeated runs. We thus formulate this problem as predicting the distribution of the reward hacking onset step under a target training recipe.   We introduce SimHack, a simulator that learns reward hacking training dynamics from a handful of smaller-scale reference RL runs and generates counterfactual simulation runs of unseen target recipes without costly retraining. Across unseen target recipes, SimHack predicts the median onset to a relative error of 11.3% and achieves across-recipe rank correlation of 0.85, while generalizing to differences in model scale, curriculum, number of rollouts, and learning rate between reference and target recipes. As an application, we show that SimHack can guide training decisions by screening candidate RL curricula, discovering curricula over the same set of scenarios that train for 96.6% longer without hacking.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.

papers.title: Effect of Zr4+ and Sr2+ addition on morphology, surface characteristics, and corrosion behavior of a new functional Zn-based phosphate conversion coating deposited on Ti6Al4V
papers.abstract: Reduced implant failure and faster osseointegration are crucial outcomes for patients using orthopedic implants. The global market for orthopedic implants is constantly growing, with metal materials accounting for the largest share of revenue; titanium and its alloys are among the most widely used. Although these materials have excellent mechanical properties and good biocompatibility, enhancing biological response and eliminating or reducing side effects after implantation remain challenging. To this end, surface engineering of materials is constantly evolving, and phosphate coatings obtained by chemical conversion are gaining increasing interest in the biomedical field. Following preliminary studies, three Zn-Zr-Sr-based phosphate coatings were developed by chemical conversion on the surface of Ti6Al4V alloy. The influence of Zr and Sr ions on the morphology and characteristics of the zinc phosphate layer was studied. It was observed that Zr ions promote the growth of phosphate crystals, while Sr ions have a densifying effect on the zinc phosphate layer. The XRD results confirmed the presence of the phase specific to the zinc phosphate layer, namely, hopeite. At the same time, phases specific to the metal ions introduced into the phosphating solution (phosphophyllite, zinc–zirconium phosphate hydrate, strontium–zinc phosphate, and strontium hydrogen phosphate hydrate) were formed. Regarding the corrosion test results, different behaviors of the layers were observed, influenced by both their morphology and the corrosive environment in which they were tested. Compared to the uncoated titanium alloy, all samples coated with a Zn-Zr-Sr phosphate base layer showed improved corrosion resistance. Therefore, in the Ringer solution, the lowest corrosion rate was obtained for the S1 sample, decreasing from 2.94 µm/year (for Ti6Al4V) to 0.22 µm/year. Moreover, in the DPBS solution, S2 showed the best kinetic response, with a reduction in corrosion rate from 5.58 (for Ti6Al4V) to 0.16 µm/year. While in EBSS, S3 showed the lowest corrosion rate, 0.21 µm/year, compared to 0.73 µm/year for Ti6Al4V. EIS results confirmed the barrier effect of phosphate layers, by increasing impedance and resistance to ionic transfer, but also highlighted the fact that protection is influenced by the compactness of the layer, intercrystalline areas, and specific interaction with the physiological environment. Surface wettability and surface free energy were evaluated before and after immersion in the three physiological media. While all coatings exhibited enhanced hydrophilicity compared to the pristine titanium, they displayed an adaptive behavior in complex physiological fluids, depending on their specific structural and morphological features. Overall, this study elucidates the effects of Zr- and Sr ions on the morphology and characteristics of Zn-based phosphate coatings, thereby enhancing corrosion resistance.

papers.title: Effect of infill density and geometry of direct ink written 3D Ni-based electrodes on their oxygen evolution reaction performance
papers.abstract: Abstract In this work, Direct Ink Writing (DIW) is used to develop novel complex 3D electrodes for water splitting, specifically for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The main advantages of using 3D electrodes for this application are to maximise catalyst surface area and facilitate gas products evacuation. High-solids-load (79 wt%), water-based pastes based on micrometer Ni powders were processed by a sequence of DIW, sintering and NiFe electrodeposition. Three different complex geometries, i.e., two rectilinear infills (40% and 55% infill density) and one gyroid infill (50% infill density), were developed as proof of concept to determine the influence of the electrode design on the OER performance. The study has demonstrated that lower infill rates (40% rectilinear infill) clearly enable OER efficiency optimisation. In addition to the higher mesh size, the superior performance of this particular electrode is enhanced by the filament orientation at 45° to the gravity vector, which facilitates buoyancy-driven bubble release, and by the inner porosity of the filaments, which is expected to favour the electrode wettability and aerophobicity.

papers.title: Deep learning assessment of rural rooftop solar potential and storage optimization
papers.abstract: Rapid deployment of distributed rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems can substantially reshape distribution-level net load and increase the likelihood of reverse power flow, making spatially explicit resource assessment and demand-side flexibility increasingly important. This study develops a bottom-up framework integrating multi-source remote sensing, deep-learning-based rooftop segmentation, geometric correction, spatiotemporal PV-potential estimation, net-load screening, and household PV-battery energy storage system (PV-BESS) scheduling for rural Qingdao, China. On the internal validation set, SegFormer outperformed U-Net and supported regional mapping of 282.04 km 2 of projected rooftop area, of which 127.34 km 2 was estimated to be technically usable. Spatial analysis showed an overall decline in building and PV-potential density with increasing distance from urban centers. City-scale and 443-household cohort analyses showed progressively deeper midday net-load troughs and reverse-power-flow conditions at higher PV penetration levels; these results are interpreted as planning-level screening rather than feeder operating-limit verification. A 24-h receding-horizon MILP-based model predictive control framework was then applied over a 153-day heating-season household dataset to evaluate coordinated PV-BESS operation across low-, medium-, and high-load groups. The 5-, 8-, and 10-kWh configurations served as reference storage cases for the three groups under the tested assumptions, while additional sensitivity analyses showed that rooftop estimates and PV-BESS performance depend on geometric, tariff, technology-cost, and irradiance assumptions. The proposed framework provides an evidence-bounded basis for spatially differentiated rooftop-PV planning and demand-side flexibility assessment in rural energy transitions.

papers.title: Research on Path Planning Method Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: This article introduces a mixed deep reinforcement learning path planning framework (DRL-PP) for self-driving cars. It's designed to be efficient, safe, and verifiable in complex, dynamic settings. The framework is built on layered action representation: the policy network gives out multi-step reference waypoints, and the lower level uses MPC/PID to make sure things are physically possible. The reward function is designed in a combined way and adds a distance-based cubic booster to amplify learning signals when getting close to the goal. The training strategy uses a dual-network setup, experience replay, and a cautious ε-cooling schedule to improve convergence stability and sample usage. During operation, it adds Action Shield and constraint projections based on control barrier functions or quadratic programming for real-time safety fixes. Compared with baseline systems like DQN and Actor–Critic on a unified grid obstacle simulation platform, the proposed method shows clear advantages in success rate, crash rate, path smoothness, and sample efficiency (example results: 94.2% success rate, 3.1% crash rate, around 3.2×10^4 exploration iterations needed to reach stable performance).

papers.title: Human-in-the-loop preference calibration for home energy management via LLM-enabled contract-constrained language interfaces
papers.abstract: As residential energy systems become increasingly electrified and coordination-intensive, home energy management systems (HEMS) must operate economically while remaining aligned with evolving user-authorized comfort and service boundaries. Existing personalization approaches rely on questionnaire initialization, fixed preference parameters, or indirect behavioral corrections, limiting alignment under changing needs and the use of runtime natural-language feedback for long-horizon calibration. This paper proposes a large language model (LLM)-enabled human-in-the-loop framework that converts user utterances into authorization-aware, contract-constrained, machine-checkable events for downstream control and preference updating. The LLM is a contract-constrained semantic interface, not a direct controller. Explicit intents support bounded execution and direct profile correction, whereas vague feedback requires option negotiation and user confirmation before bounded updating. A Contract-Informed Preference Update (CIPU) mechanism combines structured interaction evidence with projection and trust-region stabilization, while model predictive control remains the safety-constrained execution layer. In simulations, the proposed method reduces normalized preference distance by 22.50% and complaints by 74.46% relative to Survey MPC across three role-conditioned profiles. On a controlled 188-utterance language-interface benchmark, the proposed interface achieves 100% structured-event exact match and a 0% parser-level false direct-execution rate. Closed-loop ablations show 59.40% fewer complaints than the explicit-only variant, while event-log auditing of the no-contract-gate variant yields a 36.90% event-interface mismatch rate after gate removal. Under mid-horizon preference drift, final preference mismatch is reduced by 44.09% on average and up to 71.43% relative to Survey MPC.

papers.title: Intelligent photoelectric dry separation for low-rank coal upgrading
papers.abstract: Air dense medium fluidized bed (ADMFB) dry separation represents a key technology for achieving the clean and efficient utilization of coal resources. However, it still faces critical technical bottlenecks, including the difficulty of online identification of mismatched materials and the lagging regulation of separation parameters. In this study, an intelligent separation control strategy integrating an improved YOLOv13 model with Model Predictive Control (MPC) is proposed, and a closed-loop control framework of “visual perception–feature quantification–MPC decision–parameter execution” is established. A dual-channel image dataset of dry separation products, termed ADMFB-G3K , was constructed, covering separation conditions under six representative combinations of operating parameters. An improved target detection algorithm, SCU-YOLOv13, was developed by integrating a Lightweight Multi-Head Self-Attention module (LMHSA), a Multi-Scale Convolution–Attention Fusion module (MSCAF), and an Adaptive Intersection-over-Union loss function (AIoU). The LMHSA module reduced computational complexity by 68 % while improving recall by 3.5 %; the MSCAF module increased mAP@0.5 by 5.5 %; and the AIoU loss reduced bounding-box localization error by 40.2 %. Through the synergistic effect of the three modules, the model achieved a precision of 93.4 %, a recall of 92.5 %, and an mAP@0.5 of 97.8 %. Furthermore, an intelligent regulation system based on Model Predictive Control was established, in which the MPC controller was designed with a prediction horizon of Np = 20 and a control horizon of Nc = 10 . Experimental results demonstrate that MPC regulation increased the clean-coal yield by 1.79 %, reduced the ash content of clean coal to 9.97 %, and increased the ash content of tailings to 59.64 %. The probable error E p ​ decreased from 0.080 g/cm 3 under conventional open-loop/manual control to 0.065 g/cm 3 under the MPC closed-loop baseline, and further to 0.055 g/cm 3 after coordinated multi-variable optimization, and the control response time was shortened from 25-35 s to 8–12 s. In addition, the dynamic migration behavior of sulfur during the separation process was revealed. During the steady-state separation stage, the sulfur content in the upper layer decreased to 0.89–0.91 % , whereas the sulfur concentration in the lower layer reached 19.41–19.42 % , representing a 4.4-fold increase relative to the raw coal. After separation, the clean coal exhibited an ash content of 9.97 % and a sulfur content of 0.81 % , with a yield of 75.36 % ; the gangue product showed an ash content of 59.64 % and a sulfur content of 19.43 % , with a yield of 24.64 % , and the probable error E p was 0.055 g/cm 3 . These results demonstrate that high-precision intelligent dry separation of low-rank coal can be effectively achieved.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of data, features, and modeling approaches for estimating remaining driving range in electric vehicle
papers.abstract: Assessing a vehicle’s remaining driving range (RDR) is essential for alleviating range anxiety, improving energy management, and supporting sustainable mobility in public spaces for electric vehicles (EVs). Recent advancements in data-driven modeling have transformed approaches to RDR estimation, moving from conventional rule-based methods for intelligent systems capable of learning complex relationships among driving styles, battery dynamics, and interactions with external environments. Several studies have demonstrated that using real-time sensor data in conjunction with machine learning (ML) and Deep learning (DL) models enhances the accuracy of RDR estimation and captures the multifaceted relationships among driving speed, acceleration, temperature, road topology, and state-of-charge (SoC) variables. In addition to accuracy, interpretability and trustworthiness remain significant challenges, highlighting the need for causal inference and uncertainty quantification as an essential component in the development of future predictive systems.

papers.title: Probabilistic fatigue reliability assessment of girth-weld surface cracks in API 5L X65 offshore pipelines under cyclic global bending using a Kriging surrogate
papers.abstract: Fatigue cracking at girth welds threatens offshore-pipeline integrity and requires uncertainty in flaw size, crack-growth behaviour, loading and weld geometry to be considered. A probabilistic fatigue-reliability framework is developed for a semi-elliptical surface crack in an API 5L X65 pipeline under cyclic global bending. Geometry-consistent stress-intensity-factor histories from a three-dimensional finite-element model provide 60 training and six case-wise held-out simulations. The Paris-law and loading distributions are identified as DNV code-calibrated benchmark inputs, not site-specific X65 measurements. For the fixed Paris exponent, normalisation by CeffΔσeq3 reduces the primary surrogate to a one-dimensional Gaussian process in initial crack depth. The model achieves R2 = 0.997 and MAPE = 4.04% on the test cases, and R2 = 0.996 with MAPE = 3.70% in leave-one-out validation. Using conditionally truncated inputs, the posterior-mean life distribution has a median of 6.84 × 108 cycles and a 95%-reliability design life of 2.12 × 108 cycles. Correlated latent-GP posterior-function propagation gives Pf = 4.147% at Nd = 2 × 108 cycles, with a 95% GP-posterior interval of 3.858–4.444%. Sensitivity analysis identifies the stress-range scale as dominant, showing that site-specific loading characterisation is essential for field application.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Carbon Nanotechnology for Drug Delivery and Antimicrobial Therapy: From Carbon Dots and Carbon Nanotubes to Biomass-Derived Nanocarbons
papers.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and nanotechnology is emerging as a transformative approach for the design, synthesis, optimization, characterization, and biomedical application of advanced nanomaterials. Among the different classes of nanomaterials investigated for pharmaceutical applications, carbon-based nanomaterials-including carbon dots (CDs), graphene oxide (GO), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), carbon nanoparticles, porous carbon materials, and biomass-derived nanocarbons-have attracted increasing attention because of their tunable surface chemistry, high specific surface area, adsorption capacity, optical properties, electrical characteristics, and potential for surface functionalization. These characteristics make carbon- based nanomaterials attractive platforms for drug delivery, antimicrobial therapy, cancer treatment, imaging, sensing, and theranostic applications. Nevertheless, the development of carbon-based nanomedicines remains challenging because nanoparticle performance is controlled by numerous interacting variables associated with the carbon precursor, synthesis conditions, surface chemistry, particle size, morphology, drug properties, formulation parameters, and biological environment. Conventional trial-and-error optimization is therefore often inefficient and may require a large number of experiments. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), Bayesian optimization, molecular modeling, and automated experimentation, provides an opportunity to transform this process from empirical optimization into a predictive and data-driven workflow. Recent studies have demonstrated that ML can optimizesis, identify important synthesis parameters, predict optical properties, accelerate experimental development, and assist in the design of antibacterial carbon on dots [1-5]. Carbon nanomaterials also have substantial potential in pharmaceutical drug delivery. Carbon nanotubes can act as functionalized carriers for therapeutic molecules [6], while carbon dots offer small size, surface functionality, aqueous dispersibility, and multifunctional biomedical properties [2,7]. Biomass-derived carbon nanomaterials provide an additional dimension by connecting nanomedicine with sustainability and agricultural-waste valorization [16,20]. This is particularly relevant to antimicrobial therapy in low-resource environments, where the combination of inexpensive biomass-derived carbon, conventional antibiotics, and Al-guided formulation optimization could potentially contribute to locally adaptable drug-delivery technologies [16,17]. This review critically examines the integration of AI with carbon-based nanotechnology, with particular emphasis on drug delivery and antimicrobial therapy. The review discusses AI-assisted synthesis optimization, prediction of particle size and surface characteristics, drug-loading prediction, release modeling, antimicrobial activity prediction, toxicity assessment, molecular simulation, explainable AI, sustainable biomass-derived carbon, and the potential use of azithromycin-loaded carbon nanoparticles as a model antimicrobial system. The review further proposes an integrated framework in which biomass composition, synthesis conditions, nanocarrier characteristics, drug descriptors, pharmaceutical performance, antimicrobial activity, and I to toxicity are combined into a multi objective AI model. Finally, the major challenges of data scarcity, standardization, model interpretability, external validation, biological complexity, scalability, and regulatory translation are discussed. The integration of Al with sustainable carbon nanotechnology may ultimately enable a transition from trial-and-error formulation development toward predictive, explainable, economical, and environmentally responsible nanomedicine.

papers.title: Shadow fading-aided path loss modeling in street canyons at 18 GHz
papers.abstract: Accurate propagation modeling is essential for network planning and performance evaluation. This paper presents a measurement-based analysis of large-scale path loss (PL) and shadow fading (SF) at 18 GHz in a line-of-sight (LoS) street-canyon scenario, using three receiver heights. Several PL models are evaluated, and a height-dependent close-in model (CI-H) is identified as a suitable baseline, achieving a global root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.48 dB while preserving physical interpretability. Based on CI-H, SF is extracted and statistically characterized, exhibiting near-zero mean and a global standard deviation of 2.47 dB, with increasing variability at larger distances. Using the spatial structure of SF, spatial interpolation and machine-learning (ML) models are tested under both dense-route interpolation and spatially blocked validation. Under random grouped interpolation, Ordinary Kriging (OK) and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) reduce the PL RMSE to 1.35 dB and 1.21 dB, respectively. When continuous 5–20 m route segments are excluded, GPR yields 2.21–2.38 dB, improving upon the corresponding 2.51–2.53 dB CI-H values by 0.15–0.32 dB. Under nested spatial cross-validation, GPR yields 2.32 dB, 0.21 dB below the 2.53 dB CI-H baseline. Thus, the large gains obtained with nearby measurements decrease substantially as spatial separation increases, although GPR retains a modest and consistent advantage on unseen route segments.

papers.title: Enhancing Amphibious Flipper‐Based Locomotion Through Terrain‐Dependent Bayesian Optimization of Central Pattern Generator Control
papers.abstract: Sea turtles use flippers to locomote across aquatic and terrestrial environments despite substantially different mechanical demands. This multimodal capability motivates amphibious robots that can exploit flipper‐based propulsion across heterogeneous terrains, but gait performance depends strongly on environmental conditions. Here, we investigate terrain‐dependent flipper locomotion using a sea turtle–inspired robot controlled by a Hopf central pattern generator (H‐CPG). The controller parametrizes gait timing, oscillator amplitude, coupling, and stroke amplitudes for the foreflippers, hindflippers, and hip joints. We first perform simulation‐based sensitivity analysis to determine how CPG parameters affect forward speed and cost of transport across multiple environments using diagonal and synchronous coordination. We then employ multiobjective Bayesian optimization to identify terrain‐ and gait‐specific controllers that balance speed and energetic cost. Optimized controllers are transferred to hardware through a simulation‐guided, hardware‐calibrated workflow and evaluated across rigid, sandy, rocky, inclined, and aquatic testbeds. Hardware experiments show that diagonal coordination improves forward progression and electrical cost of transport across terrestrial, granular, rocky, and inclined terrains, whereas synchronous coordination performs better in water. These results demonstrate that effective amphibious locomotion requires terrain‐dependent gait selection and parameter tuning rather than a single fixed coordination pattern, providing design insights for bioinspired amphibious robots operating in heterogeneous environments.

papers.title: School Meal Programs and Student Learning Motivation: A Qualitative Case Study in Indonesia
papers.abstract: Although school meal programs are widely associated with nutritional and health benefits, their relationship with students’ learning motivation remains underexplored across diverse educational contexts. This study examines how Indonesia's Free Nutritious Meals (Free Nutritious Meals/MBG) program relates to students' learning motivation at SMA Gama Yogyakarta. Employing a qualitative case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation and analyzed using an interactive analytical approach. The findings indicate that the program is perceived to support students' learning focus, reduce classroom lethargy, and contribute to more consistent school attendance. Adequate meal provision appears to function as an external support for daily academic engagement. However, menu variations and inconsistent meal distribution schedules present challenges to the program's sustained implementation. These findings suggest that school meal programs may support a more active learning environment when nutritional provision is accompanied by reliable logistical management. The study contributes context-specific evidence to discussions of school nutrition and educational engagement, highlighting the importance of integrating food provision with consistent service delivery. Its original contribution lies in identifying the perceived links between meal provision, classroom alertness, learning focus, and attendance within a single Indonesian secondary-school case.

papers.title: Cooperative lane-changing safety under false-location injection: false safe-gap formation and risk mitigation
papers.abstract: False-location injection (FLI) can make a cooperative lane-changing system judge an unsafe target-lane gap as acceptable. This study examines how an injected location bias propagates from sensor–Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) inconsistency to fused-gap error, safety-assessment distortion, and unsafe maneuver triggering. To reduce this risk, a mitigation framework is developed by combining symmetric temporal information arbitration, Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN)-based maneuver selection, and finite-set Model Predictive Control (MPC). Simulations show that the framework reduces single-channel gap estimation errors and filters unsafe maneuver candidates under FLI attacks. Under a 50 m V2X-side FLI in the General scenario, MPC+D3QN records no observed collisions in 150 evaluation episodes, compared with collision rates of 16% for DQN, 48% for D3QN, and 100% for Pure MPC. Pure MPC remains effective in geometrically constrained scenarios, indicating a scenario-dependent benefit of the integrated controller. Coherent dual-channel spoofing produces substantially larger residual gap errors, identifying a remaining detectability boundary.

papers.title: Addressing the Engagement Blind Spot: 12-Tip Tutorial to Make Reasoning Audible in Health Professions Education
papers.abstract: Abstract Student engagement reforms have increased active learning in higher education. However, visible participation does not always require students to rehearse the spoken, interactive forms of reasoning central to professional practice, such as explaining one’s thinking, responding to challenges, building on others’ ideas, and working through uncertainty in real time. We describe this gap as an engagement blind spot. We define audible reasoning as the deliberate externalization of disciplinary or professional reasoning through spoken interaction so that its assumptions, evidence, uncertainty, and justification can be examined, challenged, revised, and developed collaboratively. It is particularly relevant in health professions education and also applies to laboratory-based and scientific disciplines where students must communicate their reasoning under conditions of uncertainty, scrutiny, and collaboration. Digital, hybrid, asynchronous, and AI-enabled learning environments sharpen this blind spot. Shared documents, online quizzes, discussion boards, and generative AI tools can support participation and access; however, they can also allow students to engage without speaking or to produce polished answers without making the underlying reasoning visible. In this context, educators need to ask not only whether students are engaged but also what behaviors they are rehearsing and whether their reasoning is available for examination and development. This tutorial offers 12 practical, evidence-informed tips developed iteratively from recurring challenges encountered in teaching, curriculum design, and faculty development and refined against selected literature. The tips are organized around 4 clusters covering the design of activities that require audible reasoning, the elicitation of reasoning in practice, the development of reasoning through listening and response, and the preservation of audible reasoning in digital and AI-enhanced environments. Across these 4 clusters, we suggest small but intentional shifts that help educators move from silent, constructive tasks toward audible, dialogic, and professionally relevant participation. These include designing tasks around uncertainty, creating low-stakes opportunities for spoken reasoning, using digital tools to surface and organize contributions for further discussion, structuring active listening and peer feedback, reviewing group dialogue formatively, and using conversational AI as a rehearsal partner rather than an authority. These strategies require attention to psychological safety, cultural responsiveness, accessibility, equity, privacy, data governance, and ongoing monitoring. Audible reasoning is not synonymous with speaking more, volunteering more frequently, or sounding fluent. Designing for audible reasoning is not simply an engagement strategy. It is a way of helping students practice the communicative and collaborative behaviors needed to explain, defend, question, and revise human judgment in clinical, scientific, and other professional contexts.

papers.title: تحليل استراتيجيات تعليم اللغة العربية وطرقه في ضوء المنهج المستقل بمدرسة لقمان الحكيم
papers.abstract: This study analyzes the strategies and methods used to teach Arabic in light of the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum (Kurikulum Merdeka) in Grade VIII at SMP IT Luqmanul Hakim, Sei Mencirim, and examines how the teacher adapts them to students' characteristics and needs. The study starts from the premise that the flexibility of the Merdeka Curriculum gives teachers considerable room for innovation, yet research on how Arabic teachers make use of this flexibility remains limited. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation in two female classes between November 2025 and May 2026, analyzed with the Miles and Huberman model, and validated through source and technique triangulation. The findings show that the teacher applies three strategies, namely cooperative learning, active learning, and a communicative strategy, and uses an eclectic method that combines lecturing, question-and-answer, discussion, reading and translation, and role play. The teacher also adapts her teaching by considering learning styles, using varied media, applying differentiated learning, and forming heterogeneous groups that support peer teaching. These practices, however, align only partially with the principles of the Merdeka Curriculum: instruction remains closely tied to the textbook Duruus al-Lughah, project-based learning has not yet been implemented, and student participation is uneven. The study concludes that strengthening alignment with the curriculum requires more varied learning media and language projects connected to students' real lives.
